title: (Poly)phenols and diabetes: From effects to mechanisms by systematic multigenomic analysis.
authors: Farrim, Maria Ines; Gomes, Andreia; Menezes, Regina; Milenkovic, Dragan
one_liner_zh: 该文通过多基因组分析研究多酚对糖尿病的调控网络，并含少量TF-代谢物分子对接，但核心是代谢疾病机制而非TF-DNA互作建模，方法以生信和对接为主，与课题关联较弱。
abstract: Diabetes is a chronic and multifactorial metabolic disease with increasing numbers of patients worldwide, characterized by loss of pancreatic beta-cell mass and function with subsequent insulin deficiency. Thus, restoring functional beta-cells could significantly impact disease management. The beneficial effects of natural compounds, namely (poly)phenols, in diabetes have gained increasing interest, due to their pleiotropic actions in several cellular processes, including in glucose homeostasis. These compounds are able to modulate nutri(epi)genomic mechanisms by interacting with cell signaling proteins and transcription factors (TFs). However, the underlying mechanisms of action, particularly of (poly)phenol metabolites resulting from digestion and colonic microbiota action, are yet to be elucidated. This study explored the multigenomic effects of (poly)phenols and their metabolites to uncover modulatory networks and mechanisms linked to diabetes. Published studies on gene expression alterations modulated by (poly)phenolic compounds or (poly)phenol-rich extracts were integrated, encompassing studies conducted on individuals with diabetes, animal models mimicking diabetes, and pancreatic beta-cell lines. Bioinformatic analysis identified differentially expressed genes and potential regulatory factors, with roles in cell signaling pathways (FoxO, AMPK, p53), endocrine resistance, immune system pathways, apoptosis, and cellular senescence. Interestingly, in silico 3D docking analyses revealed potential interactions between key TFs (FOXO1, PPARG, SIRT1, and MAFA) and some metabolites. Apigenin, luteolin, and naringenin glucuronide forms showed the best binding capacity to SIRT1. The integrative analysis of (poly)phenol metabolites data highlights the potential of these molecules for nutraceutical/pharmaceutical development aimed at managing diabetes whose incidence increases with age.
abstract_zh: 糖尿病是一种慢性、多因素代谢性疾病，全球患者数量不断增加，其特征是胰腺β细胞质量和功能丧失，进而导致胰岛素缺乏。因此，恢复功能性β细胞可能对疾病管理产生显著影响。天然化合物，即（多）酚类，在糖尿病中的有益作用因其在多种细胞过程中的多效性作用（包括葡萄糖稳态）而日益受到关注。这些化合物能够通过与细胞信号蛋白和转录因子（TFs）相互作用来调节营养（表观）基因组机制。然而，其潜在的作用机制，特别是由消化和结肠微生物群作用产生的（多）酚代谢物的机制，尚待阐明。本研究探讨了（多）酚及其代谢物的多基因组效应，以揭示与糖尿病相关的调控网络和机制。整合了已发表的关于（多）酚类化合物或富含（多）酚提取物调节基因表达变化的研究，涵盖了对糖尿病患者、模拟糖尿病的动物模型以及胰腺β细胞系进行的研究。生物信息学分析识别出差异表达基因和潜在调控因子，这些因子在细胞信号通路（FoxO、AMPK、p53）、内分泌抵抗、免疫系统通路、细胞凋亡和细胞衰老中发挥作用。有趣的是，计算机三维对接分析揭示了关键转录因子（FOXO1、PPARG、SIRT1和MAFA）与某些代谢物之间的潜在相互作用。芹菜素、木犀草素和柚皮素葡萄糖醛酸形式显示出对SIRT1的最佳结合能力。（多）酚代谢物数据的整合分析突显了这些分子在开发针对糖尿病（其发病率随年龄增长而增加）的营养保健品/药物方面的潜力。
